method: Blind read of 15 anonymous A/B pairs against packages/ai/src/tasks/language/skill-levels.prompt.md: earliest CEFR level at which the learner can handle the situation as named and described, judged by complexity (predictability, how much to understand/say/explain/adapt, language demands) rather than topic, and skills compared with each other so an easier situation never sits above a harder one in the same band. Only the skills where A and B disagree were judged. A disagreement counts as an error only where the CEFR global scale in the prompt, a well-known CEFR descriptor, or an inversion against another skill in the same output shows it; otherwise it is recorded as defensible either way. Every placement on both sides fell inside its band, and both sides return concrete levels (A1/B2...) rather than lower/upper, so neither of those separates the sides.

disagreements.name: Answer familiar questions in English
disagreements.reason: Identity and everyday activities are the A1 global descriptor ('asks and answers simple questions about where they live, people they know'); 'familiar experiences' nudges toward A2 but does not require it.

disagreements.name: Distinguish spoken English sounds
disagreements.reason: B places hearing a sound distinction (A2) above producing the same distinctions (#2 Articulate English sounds, A1 in B). Perceiving a contrast is not harder than producing it, so B inverts an easier skill above a harder one.

disagreements.name: Complete IELTS reading gaps
disagreements.reason: Summary completion needs paraphrase recognition (B2-ish) but sentence/note completion is detail location (B1). Either is sound.

disagreements.name: Connect clauses accurately
disagreements.reason: Coordination and subordination for clear meaning is the B1 'simple connected text' threshold.

disagreements.name: Deliver an IELTS Part 2 talk
disagreements.reason: Part 2 cue cards are familiar-topic descriptions; the B1 sustained-monologue descriptor ('sustain a straightforward description as a linear sequence of points') covers it.

disagreements.name: Explain opinions aloud
disagreements.reason: 'Express a view and make its supporting reasons easy to follow' is the B1 global line ('briefly giving reasons and explanations'). B2's distinguishing line (viewpoint with advantages and disadvantages) is #15 Compare alternatives, which both put at B2. A overplaces.

disagreements.name: Infer word meanings from context
disagreements.reason: CEFR inferring descriptor at B1: 'can extrapolate the meaning of occasional unknown words from the context'. Nothing in the description asks for more.

disagreements.name: Manage IELTS listening questions
disagreements.reason: A matches the other two 'Manage IELTS' skills (B2); B matches #16 listening gaps (B1). Neither is shown wrong.

errors_A: #27 Explain opinions aloud at B2 overplaces a B1 global-scale task
#32 Infer word meanings at B2 is above the B1 CEFR descriptor
errors_B: #7 Distinguish spoken sounds at A2 sits above #2 Articulate sounds at A1 (inversion)
pairs.reason: Close. A's clearest miss (#27) contradicts the rubric's own B1 wording, and #32 is also above its CEFR descriptor; B's clearest miss is the #7/#2 inversion. Leans otherwise split. B edges it on the stronger, rubric-backed calls.

disagreements.name: Recognize paraphrases in texts
disagreements.reason: Text paraphrase below audio paraphrase (#5, B2 in both) is coherent; B2 is also sound.

disagreements.name: Repair unclear spoken responses
disagreements.reason: CEFR B1 repair/compensation ('correct mix-ups', 'use a simple word meaning something similar') already covers rephrasing and recovering.

disagreements.name: Select key features of visuals
disagreements.reason: Mostly analytical selection feeding #19 (B2 in both); either level is arguable.

disagreements.name: Support claims with reasons and examples
disagreements.reason: Reasons plus concrete examples is the B1 'briefly giving reasons and explanations' line; it does not ask for weighing alternatives.

disagreements.name: Follow arguments in academic texts
disagreements.reason: Following claims, reasons and counterpoints in demanding texts is C1 ('understands a wide range of demanding, longer texts'). C2 is 'virtually everything with ease'.

disagreements.name: Identify a writer's stance
disagreements.reason: Telling assertion from reported or hedged claims is C1 'recognizes implicit meaning'.

disagreements.name: Qualify and defend spoken views
disagreements.reason: Near-duplicate of #22 'Develop and defend answers to Part 3 questions', which B itself puts at C1. B splits the same situation across levels.

disagreements.name: Revise IELTS writing responses
disagreements.reason: Checking one's own report/essay against criteria is not harder than writing it (#34 Task 2 essays, C1 in B); C2 inverts revision above production.

disagreements.name: Weigh arguments and concessions
disagreements.reason: Comparing views with concessions while holding a position is C1 well-structured argument; B places it above #34 writing the argument essay (C1).

errors_B: #31 at C2 while near-duplicate #22 is C1
#32 and #33 at C2 above #34 Write Task 2 essays at C1
pushes 5 of 15 C-band skills to C2 for ordinary academic-IELTS tasks
pairs.reason: Same B-band disagreements are mild leans, but B's C2 placements contradict its own C1 placements of near-identical or harder skills. A is internally consistent.

disagreements.name: Perguntar quanto é o aluguel
disagreements.reason: 'How much is...?' is A1; understanding what the rent includes leans A2. Both stay below #3 lease comprehension (A2).

disagreements.name: Perguntar sobre a vaga e a equipe
disagreements.reason: Prepared questions and answers about concrete work matters fit B1 ('main points of clear standard speech on familiar matters at work').

disagreements.name: Relacionar suas habilidades à vaga
disagreements.reason: Close to #12 'connect your experience to the job' (B1 in both); A splits two similar situations, though #32 does add adapting to what the interviewer said.

errors_A: #32 at B2 while similar #12 is B1 (weak)
errors_B: #30 at B2 is a likely overplacement (weak)
pairs.reason: One weak lean each, no substantiated error on either side.

disagreements.name: Reconhecer sons da fala espanhola
disagreements.reason: Sound recognition is foundational (A1) but segmenting the speech flow can be A2.

disagreements.name: Adequar o registro escrito
disagreements.reason: CEFR sociolinguistic B2 is confident formal/informal register; adjusting greeting and tú/usted is B1-level convention. Either fits the description.

disagreements.name: Analisar argumentos na fala
disagreements.reason: Separating thesis from justifications and examples in interviews and talks is B2 ('complex lines of argument'). A puts it below #14, the same analysis in writing (B2), though real-time speech is not easier than text.

errors_A: #15 spoken argument analysis at B1 below written argument analysis #14 at B2
pairs.reason: Only #15 separates them, in B's favor.

disagreements.name: Interpretar imagens oralmente no B2
disagreements.reason: Describing a situation beyond a list of objects is B1 description; interpreting and speculating leans B2. The exam name in the title should not decide it.

disagreements.name: Reformular ideias oralmente
disagreements.reason: B1 compensation (simple substitute word) vs B2 circumlocution and self-correction of ambiguity; the description sits between them.

pairs.reason: Two borderline skills, each defensible on both sides.

disagreements.name: Catch numbers and spelled details
disagreements.reason: A1 listening covers numbers, prices and times spoken slowly; 'accurately' and spelled names push slightly but not clearly to A2.

disagreements.name: Distinguish spoken English sounds
disagreements.reason: B again puts hearing a distinction (A2) above producing it (#2, A1 in B).

disagreements.name: Connect clauses accurately
disagreements.reason: Mirrors #36: each side places one of clause-linking/sentence-linking at B2. Neither pairing is clearly wrong.

disagreements.name: Deliver an IELTS Part 2 talk
disagreements.reason: B1 sustained description of a familiar topic.

disagreements.name: Explain opinions aloud
disagreements.reason: B1 global-scale wording; A overplaces.

disagreements.name: Follow connected English speech
disagreements.reason: B1 is 'clear, standard speech'; reduced sounds at natural speed is the B2 native-speaker conversation line.

disagreements.name: Label diagrams from passages
disagreements.reason: Matching labels to stated information is detail location, like #37 (B1 in both).

disagreements.name: Link ideas across sentences
disagreements.reason: See #18.

disagreements.name: Manage IELTS listening questions
disagreements.reason: As in p1.

errors_A: #29 Follow natural-speed reduced speech at B1 underplaces
pairs.reason: A has two well-supported errors in opposite directions (#27 up, #29 down) plus leans against it on #19 and #34; B's main miss is the #7 inversion.

disagreements.name: Recognize paraphrases in audio
disagreements.reason: Matching question wording to different words heard once at speed is harder than the text version (#6, B1 in both); A flattens them, B separates them and matches #9 listening answers (B2).

disagreements.name: Repair unclear spoken responses
disagreements.reason: B1 repair/compensation.

disagreements.name: Support claims with reasons and examples
disagreements.reason: B1 'giving reasons and explanations'.

pairs.reason: Three leans, all toward B; no hard error either side.

disagreements.name: Explicar o motivo da viagem na imigração
disagreements.reason: Purpose and length of stay is a highly predictable, formulaic exchange (A1); A2 is also reasonable.

disagreements.name: Perguntar quanto é o aluguel
disagreements.reason: As in p3.

disagreements.name: Descrever um desacordo profissional
disagreements.reason: Narrating what happened and how it was discussed is B1 'describes experiences, events... briefly giving reasons', like #20 and #35 (B1 in both).

disagreements.name: Perguntar sobre a vaga e a equipe
disagreements.reason: As in p3.

disagreements.name: Relacionar suas habilidades à vaga
disagreements.reason: As in p3.

disagreements.name: Relatar um erro e um aprendizado
disagreements.reason: Same B1 narrative-with-reasons task as #20 and #35, which A places at B1.

errors_A: #19 and #34 at B2 while equivalent work narratives #20 and #35 are B1
pairs.reason: A's two narrative overplacements are inconsistent with its own B1 placements of equivalent narratives; B's differing calls are leans.

disagreements.name: Reconhecer sons da fala espanhola
disagreements.reason: As in p4.

disagreements.name: Analisar argumentos na fala
disagreements.reason: As in p4: A places spoken argument analysis below the written version (#14, B2).

disagreements.name: Distinguir indicativo e subjuntivo
disagreements.reason: Recognizing the mood contrast (B1 in B) below producing nuance with it (#25, B2 in B) is coherent, and subjunctive transfers from Portuguese; B2 for the full range including hypotheses is also sound.

errors_A: #15 spoken argument analysis at B1 below written #14 at B2
pairs.reason: Only #15 separates them, in B's favor.

disagreements.name: Interpretar imagens oralmente no B2
disagreements.reason: As in p5.

disagreements.name: Relacionar falantes e opiniões
disagreements.reason: B1 'follow main points of extended discussion' vs B2 'keep up with animated discussion'; matching viewpoints to voices fits either.

disagreements.name: Relacionar textos e informações
disagreements.reason: CEFR B1 reading for information: 'gather information from different parts of a text, or from different texts, in order to fulfil a specific task'.

disagreements.name: Revisar a precisão de textos
disagreements.reason: Self-revision of agreement, tenses and accents is B1 accuracy work; B2 self-correction is also arguable.

errors_B: #19 at B2 is above the B1 CEFR descriptor for gathering information across texts
pairs.reason: Only #19 has descriptor support, in A's favor.

disagreements.name: Deliver an IELTS Part 2 talk
disagreements.reason: B1 sustained description of a familiar topic.

disagreements.name: Explain opinions aloud
disagreements.reason: B1 global-scale wording; B overplaces.

disagreements.name: Infer word meanings from context
disagreements.reason: B1 CEFR inferring descriptor.

disagreements.name: Link ideas across sentences
disagreements.reason: B1 cohesion ('link a series of shorter elements into a connected sequence'), matching #18 (B1 in both).

errors_A: #32 Infer word meanings at B2 is above the B1 descriptor
errors_B: #27 Explain opinions at B2 overplaces a B1 global-scale task
pairs.reason: Each has one supported miss; A also holds two leans (#19, #36).

disagreements.name: Support claims with reasons and examples
disagreements.reason: B1 'giving reasons and explanations'.

disagreements.name: Use English rhythm and intonation
disagreements.reason: CEFR phonological control: using stress, intonation and rhythm to support the intended message is the B2 descriptor; B1 is intelligible despite L1 prosody. A's split from #17 word stress (B1 in both) is principled.

errors_B: #15 at B1 below the CEFR B2 prosody descriptor it matches
pairs.reason: Both disagreements favor A, one with descriptor support.

disagreements.name: Descrever um projeto profissional
disagreements.reason: Goal, contribution and result is a B1 narrative; B puts it above #35 colaboração and #33 trajetória (B1 in B), which ask the same kind of account.

disagreements.name: Explicar uma transição profissional
disagreements.reason: Dates and clear reasons is the B1 'briefly giving reasons and explanations' line.

disagreements.name: Perguntar sobre a vaga e a equipe
disagreements.reason: As in p3.

errors_B: #20 at B2 while equivalent narratives #33 and #35 are B1
pairs.reason: All three disagreements favor A; B overplaces plain work narratives.

disagreements.name: Interpretar conectores argumentativos
disagreements.reason: Recognizing cause, contrast, purpose and consequence connectors is B1. A puts recognizing connectors (B2) above producing cohesive paragraphs with them (#10, B1 in A): a receptive skill above its productive counterpart.

disagreements.name: Relacionar falantes e opiniões
disagreements.reason: As in p10.

errors_A: #3 connector recognition at B2 above #10 cohesive paragraph writing at B1 (inversion)
pairs.reason: Only #3 is substantiated, in B's favor.

caveats: The 15 pairs are 5 distinct inputs each run three times (p1/p6/p11, p2/p7/p12, p3/p8/p13, p4/p9/p14, p5/p10/p15). Labels A and B were not checked for a stable mapping to any model, so the A/B counts should be unblinded per pair before aggregating.
Only 61 of 492 placements differ; most verdicts rest on 2 to 4 borderline skills, and 9 of the 15 verdicts are low or medium confidence.
Many disagreements are genuinely borderline (receptive vs productive, prepared vs adaptive); those are marked 'defensible' and did not decide a verdict.
Judgments use the prompt's CEFR global scale and my recall of CEFR Companion Volume descriptors; no native-speaker or examiner check.
Both sides emit concrete CEFR levels rather than the prompt's lower/upper output, identically, so that did not affect any verdict.
